title: Dense pentacene cocrystal demonstrates room-temperature coherent control
summary: Maximizing the number of addressable spins within a fixed volume can improve ensemble quantum sensor sensitivity, but dense packing usually increases dipolar interactions and excited-state transport, shortening coherence and suppressing optical readout. Here we report a 2:1 cocrystal of 6,13-dihydropentacene and pentacene (DHP/Pc) containing 33.3 mol% pentacene ($3.3\times10^{5}$ ppm; $9.51\times10^{20}$ cm$^{-3}$), a volumetric spin-site density more than two orders of magnitude above previous benchmarks, NV-diamond and pentacene-doped p-terphenyl (PDP).
